preconditions.description: The number of people in the tree, n, is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= ri <= n for ri in r) and len(r) == n
preconditions.description: The parent array r has exactly n elements, where each ri is either 0 (no parent) or a valid person index (1 ≤ ri ≤ n).
The number of queries, m, is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= vi <= n and 1 <= pi <= n for vi, pi in queries) and len(queries) == m
preconditions.description: Each query consists of a person vi (1 ≤ vi ≤ n) and a cousin degree pi (1 ≤ pi ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: not any(vi == pi for vi, pi in queries)
preconditions.description: Queries do not require counting a person as their own cousin (vi ≠ pi is implicit in the problem statement).

preconditions.expression: not any(vi == r[vi - 1] for vi in range(1, n + 1) if r[vi - 1] != 0)
preconditions.description: No person is their own direct parent (no self-loops).

preconditions.expression: not any(vi == r[vi - 1] or vi == r[r[vi - 1] - 1] for vi in range(1, n + 1) if r[vi - 1] != 0 and r[r[vi - 1] - 1] != 0)
preconditions.description: No person is their own indirect parent (no cycles of length 2).

postconditions.expression: all(len(output) == m and output[i] >= 0 for i in range(m))
postconditions.description: The output is a list of m non-negative integers, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(output[i] == sum(1 for j in range(1, n + 1) if j != vi and is_p_cousin(vi, j, p, r)) for i, (vi, pi) in enumerate(queries))
postconditions.description: For each query (vi, pi), the output is the count of people j ≠ vi who are pi-th cousins of vi, where is_p_cousin(vi, j, p, r) is true if there exists a person z such that z is a p-ancestor of both vi and j.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= p <= n and p > 0 for p in [pi for (vi, pi) in queries])
postconditions.description: The cousin degree pi in each query is a positive integer (1 ≤ pi ≤ n).

invariants.expression: all(1 <= i <= n for i in range(1, n + 1))
invariants.description: Person indices are unique and range from 1 to n.

invariants.expression: all(r[i - 1] == 0 or (1 <= r[i - 1] <= n) for i in range(1, n + 1))
invariants.description: Each person's parent is either 0 (no parent) or a valid person index.
